summary: Something your organisation sets out to achieve. Aims come in three levels: goals, the objectives under them, and the outcomes under those.
example: Goal: Raise produce quality. Objective under it: Hold every depot to one standard. Outcome under that: Depot staff apply the standard alike.
definition: An aim is something your organisation sets out to achieve, at one of three levels. A goal is a broad direction you keep working towards, such as raise produce quality. An objective is one concrete change made for a goal, such as hold every depot to one standard; it is done once it is made. An outcome is what is then true of people or things, such as depot staff apply the standard alike. Goals sit under your purpose, objectives under goals, and outcomes under objectives. An outcome closes a gap: the difference between how things are and how they should be. Numbers go in the measures, not in the aim itself. An aim is not a project (work that ends), an operation (work that continues) or a KPI (a number you track).

levels.goal: A broad direction your organisation keeps working towards.
levels.objective: One concrete change your organisation sets out to make.
levels.outcome: A fact about people or things once that change is made.

levelExamples.goal: Raise produce quality, over the cooperative's 2025 to 2028 plan.
levelExamples.objective: Hold every depot to one standard, under the goal Raise produce quality.
levelExamples.outcome: Depot staff apply the standard alike, once every depot is held to one standard.

/spec/level.guide: Goal, objective or outcome. Choose this first: it decides what the aim says and what it sits under.

/spec/parent.guide: The aim this one belongs to: a goal for an objective, an objective for an outcome. A goal sits directly under your purpose. If the aim you need does not exist yet, add it first.

outcome.guide: The objective that is met once this outcome is true.

/metadata/name.guide: A short name for the aim. For an outcome, say what will be true in a few words.
good: Season results reach members on time

poor.why: Names an activity, not an aim or a state.

/spec/objective.guide: The aim in one sentence. For a goal or objective, say what you will do and the result it is for. For an outcome, say what will be true. Leave numbers out.

goal.guide: What you will do and the long-term result it is for.
good: Raise what a member earns from a season of deliveries, by selling more of what they grow at a better price.

poor.why: The number belongs in a key result; the statement says the aim.
A topic, not an aim: no action and no result.

objective.guide: What you will do and the specific result it is for, reachable before the goal's end date.
good: Hold every depot to one quality standard, so a buyer gets the same quality from any of them.

poor.text: Hold every depot to one quality standard and train all staff and replace the scanners.
poor.why: Three aims in one sentence; each is its own objective, or the work belongs in a project.

outcome.guide: What people will see is true once the objective is met, in the present tense. Not an action.
good: A fault is caught at intake, where it can still be put right, instead of at the buyer, where it cannot.
Produce spends its first day in a depot, not in a field or on a truck.

poor.text: Reduce delivery time to customers so produce arrives fresh and service is dependable.
poor.why: This is an action with two results. Say what will be true, such as produce arrives fresh, and make dependable service its own outcome.
A target, not a state: the 90% and the 24 hours belong in a key result.

/spec/statedAs.guide: The aim word for word from the published plan it comes from. Leave it empty if the aim is your own.

/spec/source.guide: The document and the section or page the wording comes from.
good: Quality review of the 2025 spring season, section 4

/spec/keyResults.guide: How you will know the aim is met, in one to three key results; more dilutes its focus. Each key result is a number with today's figure and date, a target and date, the direction it should move, and its unit. You can link a KPI instead.

/spec/keyResults/-/metric.guide: What is counted, precisely enough that two people would count the same thing.
good: days from the season closing to results reaching members

poor.why: Not countable as written: speed of what, from when to when?

/spec/keyResults/-/kind.guide: What sort of number this is: percent, count, money, ratio or duration. A count, money or duration needs a unit; a percent or ratio takes none.

/spec/keyResults/-/unit.guide: The unit, such as lots or days. Leave it empty for a percent or a ratio.

/spec/keyResults/-/baseline.guide: Today's figure and the date it was measured. If you do not know it yet, say why; do not guess.

/spec/keyResults/-/target.guide: The figure to reach and the month to reach it by, within the aim's dates.

/spec/owner.guide: The role responsible for this aim, not a named person. If the role does not exist yet, add it first.

poor.why: A person, not a role. Pick the role this person fills.

/spec/horizon.guide: When work on this aim starts and when it should be reached.

/spec/whyItMatters.guide: What this aim changes, and for whom.
good: An inconsistent supplier is priced as its worst delivery, not its average one.

poor.why: Does not say what changes or for whom.

/spec/contributesTo.guide: Other goals or objectives this outcome also helps, and how.

Goal:/spec/parent.ask: What will show this aim is met? For a goal, its objectives; for an objective, its outcomes. Check the existing ones first.
Goal:/spec/parent.ifNone: Add them now: objectives under a goal, or outcomes under an objective. Write each outcome as what will be true, with its measures and the gap it closes.

Gap:/spec/outcomes.ask: Which gap does this outcome close? A gap is the difference between how things are now and how they should be.
Gap:/spec/outcomes.ifNone: Add the gap after you write this outcome: how things are now, how they should be, the KPI that tracks it, where it was seen, and where the evidence comes from.

checks.smart-specific: Write the aim in words, without numbers.
checks.smart-measurable: Add a key result with a target, or link a KPI that has one.
checks.smart-attainable: Give every measure today's figure, dated before its target, moving the way its direction says.
checks.smart-relevant: Place the aim under the right parent and say why it matters.
checks.smart-time-bound: Date every target, inside the horizon.
checks.horizon: Give start and end dates within the dates of the aim this one belongs to.
checks.closes-gap: Name the gap this outcome closes, or add that gap.
checks.key-results-count: Keep one to three key results. More dilutes the aim's focus.
checks.contributes-to: Link each one to a goal or objective other than the one this outcome sits under, and say how it helps.
checks.has-objectives: Define the objectives under this goal, or place existing ones under it.
checks.has-outcomes: Add outcomes under this objective, each saying what will be true, or move existing ones under it.
checks.outcomes-close-gaps: For each outcome, name the gap it closes, or add that gap.
checks.statement-state: Say what will be true once it is met, not what to do.
checks.placed: Place it under the aim it serves: an objective under a goal, an outcome under an objective. Define that first if it does not exist yet.

good.label: a state of things that will be true

poor.label: an action or task to carry out

statement-state.pass: Written as a state that will be true.
statement-state.fail: This reads as something to do. Say what will be true once it is met.
